21511-bell-s-cathedrals-the-priory-churc:
George Worley's guide to St Bartholomew-the-Great, Smithfield, came out in 1908 in Bell's Cathedral series. Worley also wrote on Southwark Cathedral and the Temple Church. His book gives a short history of the priory's founding and a full account of its fabric.

Forty-two pictures show the church, inside and out, including the view from the organ gallery. Worley points students to the great Monasticon account of the Smithfield foundation. He also treats the sister church of St Bartholomew-the-Less and the rule of the Austin canons. For walkers in old London, the book is a compact, learned companion.
2649-captains-of-the-civil-war-a-chronic:
William Wood wrote this chronicle of the Civil War's captains for the Chronicles of America series, volume 31 in the Abraham Lincoln edition. Sixty years after Fort Sumter, Wood notes, the war still stood as the third and greatest modern civil war among English speaking peoples.

The book follows generals of the Blue and the Gray, never ignoring the politics that shaped their campaigns. Wood writes for general readers, with maps of character as well as battle. The chronicle serves as a clear, compact guide to the men who led armies, and to the war that remade America.
captains-of-the-civil-war-a-chronicle-of:
William Wood wrote Captains of the Civil War for the Chronicles of America series, published by Yale in 1921, sixty years after Fort Sumter. Wood, a Canadian colonel, announces a book of warriors that never ignores the politics behind them. Chapters run from the clash of 1861 through the naval and river wars to Gettysburg, Grant's hammering of 1864, Sherman's march, and the end in 1865.

Portraits anchor the campaigns: Lincoln as war statesman, Lee and Jackson in the east, Farragut on the water, Grant on the rivers and then the front. Maps and Brady photographs serve the text. Wood writes brisk, admiring military history for general readers, treating Blue and Gray captains in one chronicle, as his subtitle promises.
doe-osti-2589162-long-duration-energy-st: Storing power for days got its DOE playbook, and this report prices the long game. The pages detail the value math. The utilities get their guide. The storage was long-duration. The math was value. The guide was utility. The playbook was DOE's.

doe-osti-3097330-cluster-dynamics-simula: Fission gas got cluster-simulated, and this DOE text models intra-granular bubbles. The pages detail the dynamics findings. The nuclear folks get their data. The evolution was pressure. The data were nuclear. The 2 were UO. The granular were intra.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-WeisbergHaroldC: Harold Weisberg titled a monograph A Citizen's Dissent, and filled it with correspondence and notes on the Kennedy killing. The name states his position: one citizen refusing the official account. Weisberg's dissent rested on documents he gathered and letters he wrote over years. The monograph gathers that material in one place, showing how his case against the Warren Commission grew out of paper, not theory alone.
nasa-tm-19650021407-gemini-launch-vehicl:
Prepared in June 1963 by the Aerospace Corporation for NASA's Gemini program office, this report covers pilot safety for the Gemini launch vehicle at the Atlantic Missile Range. Report TOR-169 was made under an Air Force contract for the Space Systems Division. Gemini would carry two astronauts on a modified military rocket.

A safety program sets the rules that protect a crew on the pad and in early flight. It also protects people on the ground below the flight path. The report records how that program was organized at the range. Such planning rarely makes headlines, but every crewed launch rested on it.
nasa-tm-19720018347-aerodynamic-characte:
Ernald B Graves of the Langley Research Center reported these orbiter tests in May 1972, as NASA TM X-2561. The model was a space shuttle orbiter with a sixty degree swept delta wing. It formed part of the shuttle systems study program. Designers needed the shape's steady aerodynamic behavior before committing to it. Some control power tests were included in the program. The work ran in the Langley Unitary Plan wind tunnel.

Three supersonic speeds anchor the data set. They are Mach 2.50, Mach 3.90, and Mach 4.60. Flow density was held at a set Reynolds number per length. The results give the static forces and moments on the model. Control effectiveness readings show how well its surfaces could steer it. Such tables fed the shuttle's early design trade studies.
the-bark-covered-house-or-back-in-the-wo:
William Nowlin published his Michigan pioneer account in 1876, after spending much of the winter of 1875 writing it. Friends who read or heard the manuscript urged him to print it in the Centennial Year. Levi Bishop of Detroit, head of a county pioneer society, backed the book.

A key outlines the lives of John and Melinda Nowlin, their journey, and their settlement in Michigan. Scenes of forest life follow, with hopes, fears, and hard work, until clearing and farming bring what the key calls harvest home. Nowlin presents pioneer soldiers winning a long fight with nature to gain a home.
the-luck-of-thirteen-wanderings-and-flig: Mr. and Mrs. Jan Gordon wrote The Luck of Thirteen: Wanderings and Flight through Montenegro and Serbia, published in New York by E. P. Dutton and Company in 1916, with photographs, a map, and colour plates. Only the title page and part of the contents are present here, so the narrative itself does not appear. Chapters shown include Nish and Salonika, Off to Montenegro, Across the Frontier, The Montenegrin Front on the Drina, Northern Montenegro, and To Cettinje. A frontispiece caption reads, Jo at the Machine Gun.
the-station-the-party-fight-and-funeral-:
This volume holds three tales by William Carleton. It is volume three, part two, of his collected works. The tales come from Traits and Stories of the Irish Peasantry. They are The Station, The Party Fight and Funeral, and The Lough Derg Pilgrim. The first opens in a chapel in Tir-neer, where the Reverend Philemy M'Guirk stands on the altar after Mass to announce the coming week's stations.

The priest calls on Jack Gallagher of Corraghnamoddagh, teasing him for seldom making part of the congregation and warning him to be prepared for Monday's station at his house. Carleton's comedy of parish life, Irish speech, and clerical banter runs through the announcement, setting the tone for the peasant tales that follow in the volume.
